title: lemma checked-program document
description: What the lemma bin prints for one input file: the program the file parses to, or why it has none. `lemma check` type checks the project first (gated: true); `lemma parse` does not (gated: false). A refused file still gets a document, so a batch reader matches every input to an answer. `schemaVersion` changes whenever a reader of an older document would misread a newer one.

file.description: The path as the caller gave it.

gated.description: Whether the program passed the typecheck gate on its way here.

script.description: The script the program was parsed from, when that is not the file's own text: the TypeScript with its types stripped. `lemma check` always carries it and `lemma parse` never does.

reason.description: Why there is no program. `unreadable` comes only from `lemma parse`: under `lemma check`, a file the type check did not read is `outside-program`, whether or not it exists.

diagnostics.description: The gate's findings, for a typecheck refusal. `file` is relative to the directory the check ran in, and absent, with `line`, for a project-level finding.
